newsitem.title: USA: Former health care employee settles SEC charges.
newsitem.headline: Former health care employee settles SEC charges.

text.p: A doctor who worked for Intergroup Healthcare Corp., a managed health care firm that merged with Foundation Health Corp. in 1994, agreed to pay more than $200,000 in connection with an insider trading case, the government said Monday.
Raeburn Evans, 49, of Chatham, N.J., did not admit or deny any wrongdoing in the case, the Securities and Exchange Commission said.

In a complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Washington, the SEC alleged that Evans learned about Intergroup Healthcare's merger negotiations in his post as medical director for the company's southern region.
The agency said Evans, before any public announcements about the pending deal, bought common stock and purchased and sold Intergroup options leading to illegal gains of $109,003.
The $200,000 payment includes the alleged illegal profits and a civil penalty, the agency said. An attorney representing Evans declined to comment on the settlement.
